title: Bag of Tokens
summary: You start with a given power and a score of zero, along with a set of tokens represented by an integer array.
statement: You start with a given power and a score of zero, along with a set of tokens represented by an integer array. Each token has a specific value. Your goal is to maximize your score by playing tokens in one of two ways: face-up or face-down. For a face-up play, if your current power is at least equal to the token's value, you can play the token, reducing your power by the token's value but increasing your score by one. For a face-down play, if your score is at least one, you can play the token, increasing your power by the token's value but decreasing your score by one. The task is to determine the maximum score you can achieve by playing any number of tokens.
constraints: Spend power to play a token face up for one score, or spend one score to play it face down for power.
Each token is used at most once; return maximum score reached.
hints: When buying, cheapest preserves power; when selling, largest maximizes the next opportunity.
Sort and maintain low/high pointers, current score, and best score.
Buy low when possible; otherwise sell high only with positive score.
Exchange arguments show these extremes dominate any other face-up or face-down choice.
editorial: Exchange arguments show these extremes dominate any other face-up or face-down choice.

Buy 100, sell 400, then buy 200 and 300 to reach score two.
